newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Long Australia bonds test resistance on sale.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Long Australia bonds test resistance on sale.

text.p: *Australian bonds firmed after a good response to a T-bond tender and comments by Treasurer Costello that were seen as downplaying perceptions that the RBA had ruled out a rate cut.
*Focus now on Thursday's labour force report.

Australian bonds firmed after a positive response to a A$700 million Treasury bond tender, which was viewed as a good test for the market after the recent shake-out which saw the long-end brush 8.0 percent yields.

The March 10-year bond futures contract ended the session testing key resistance at 92.210, a level that capped the market in after hours trading, and where a break could see the market squeeze up to 92.340, analysts said.
Fuelling the positive tone going into the close were comments by Treasurer Peter Costello that were seen as downplaying perceptions that the RBA had ruled out a rate cut.
Asked by a reporter whether the Reserve Bank had been premature in "ruling out" a monetary policy easing, Costello said the bank had not said that.
"I don't think the bank said that. I think what the bank said, as I recall, in its quarterly Bulletin, was that monetary policy was appropriate," he said.
"Now you can read whatever you want into that," he said.
Since the Bulletin in February yields have been on an upward track amid signs of an economic rebound, which had been viewed as underpinning the RBA's now 'on hold' policy stance.
December bill futures, while mildly firmer on the day, are still pricing in a 75 basis point tightening in current 6.0 percent official interest rates by the end of the year.

"The Federal Reserve is going to tighten some time fairly soon...and here everybody is pretty much convinced that the Reserve Bank is going to lag the Fed by about six months," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.
The next key focus for the market will be Thursday's labour force report for February.

The local positive tone saw the initial underperformance against the U.S. reversed. The 10-year spread to the U.S. has now returned to a level seen prior to Friday's sharp pre-U.S. non-farm payrolls sell-off, but a further contraction is expected to hang on the outcome of this Thursday's data.
-- Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
